corrected_content.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations $R_{1}:=R_{1} + (-1)R_{2}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2} + (-2)R_{1}$?

$$
A = \left[ \begin{array}{cc}5 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{array} \right] , \hspace{2em} B = \left[ \begin{array}{cc}- 2 & 1 \\ - 1 & 1\end{array} \right] , \hspace{2em} C = \left[ \begin{array}{cc}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{array} \right]
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Apply the two operations in the stated order, using the new first row in the second operation.

$$
A:\quad\begin{bmatrix}5 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$



$$
B:\quad\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$



$$
C:\quad\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\sim\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Only $C$ becomes the identity matrix.
